application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description: TG1 NE Boundary fence line, under crown of willow.- Remove dead tree - Cut back all ivy and growth hard backT2 Early mature Weeping Willow - Reduce to approx. 3.5m in height- Small fruit tree under Willow - lightly reduce tip ends to form a rounded and shapely framework TG3 Fence line on Northern boundary - Remove dead wood from Mulberry tree - Cut back all ivy and growth hard back to to fence line to tidy- Goat Willow - Crown lift to approx. 4m over client garden sideTG4 Group of 4 x Apple and 1 x plum in centre of garden next to path- Sensitively reduce each tree with emphasis on longer protruding growth to create rounded form for uniform regrowth TG5 Two previously reduced mature established apple trees - Reduce each tree back to vicinity of previous pruning points- Trim Ivy back to fenceT6 Small bay tree with long main leader in centre top - Remove leader from top of tree and prune over to maintain rounded shapeTG7 Growth on fence line on northern boundary, mainly mature Rose - Reduce back fence line to reduce encroachment towards raised vegetable bedsT8 Large apple tree on narrow part of garden next to boundary fence - Reduce all over to a rounded framework reducing by approximately 0.5m past previous reduction pointsT9 Dead stem benched on fence post originated from neighbour's garden - Reduce down to 1.5m to height of bamboo, to prevent risk of failing unexpectantly T10 Large Greengauge next to post with hose - Reduce over by approximately 1.5-2mT11 Mature apple tree next to washing line- Reduce over by approximately 1.5-2mT12 Bay tree located behind T11 (in neighbour's garden)- Reduce height by approximately 3m to reduce encroachment issues and increase light levelsT13 Pear tree (in neighbour's garden)- Reduce height by approximately 3m to reduce encroachment issues and increase light levels
